recipe: (React 19.2+) Replace conditional rendering like `{isShowing && <Panel />}` with `<Activity mode={isShowing ? 'visible' : 'hidden'}>` when a hidden component must keep its state for when it reappears.
trigger_condition: You are conditionally showing/hiding a component and need its internal state (useState, etc.) to survive the hide/show cycle.
evidence: When you hide a component using an Activity boundary instead, React will "save" its state for later
_original_recipe: Replace conditional rendering (e.g., `isShowing && <Component />`) with an Activity boundary when you need to hide a component but preserve its internal state for later restoration.

recipe: (React 19.2+) Activity hides children with display: none, so their DOM (e.g. uncontrolled textarea contents) survives too. Wrap tab panels in Activity to keep that ephemeral state across tab switches.
trigger_condition: You have multiple UI sections (like tabs) with uncontrolled inputs whose DOM state you want to retain when the user navigates away and back.
evidence: Since Activity boundaries hide their children using `display: none`, their children's DOM is also preserved when hidden. This makes them great for maintaining ephemeral state in parts of the UI that the user is likely to interact with again.
_original_recipe: Wrap tab-based UI sections in Activity boundaries to preserve uncontrolled DOM state (e.g., textarea content) when switching between tabs.
_review_reason: missing React 19.2+ qualifier; state the display:none mechanism from the evidence

recipe: (React 19.2+) Pre-render content the user will likely need next inside `<Activity mode="hidden">`; it loads its code and data ahead of time and appears faster when switched to visible.
trigger_condition: You know the user will soon navigate to a section of content and want to reduce its loading time when it becomes visible.
evidence: This _pre-rendering_ allows the children to load any code or data they need ahead of time, so that later, when the Activity boundary becomes visible, the children can appear faster with reduced loading times.
_original_recipe: Pre-render content that will likely be needed soon by wrapping it in `<Activity mode="hidden">`, so it loads code and data ahead of time and appears faster when made visible.

recipe: Wrap components that the user is likely to navigate to next in Activity boundaries with mode='hidden' so they pre-render and fetch their data before becoming visible, reducing perceived loading time.
trigger_condition: You have a UI with multiple sections (e.g., tabs) where switching between them causes a loading delay because the target component hasn't been mounted yet.
evidence: Pre-rendering components with hidden Activity boundaries is a powerful way to reduce loading times for parts of the UI that the user is likely to interact with next.

recipe: Wrap independent parts of your component tree in Activity boundaries to enable Selective Hydration, allowing React to hydrate some parts (like tab buttons) before others (like the tab content) finish loading.
trigger_condition: Your server-rendered page contains multiple independent sections and you want some parts to become interactive before the entire page finishes hydrating.
evidence: Since Activity boundaries show and hide their children, they already naturally divide the component tree into independent units. And just like Suspense, this feature allows them to participate in Selective Hydration.

recipe: (React 19.2+) Activity boundaries take part in Selective Hydration like Suspense. Even if you never hide anything, wrapping independent regions in always-visible Activity boundaries lets React hydrate them as separate units.
trigger_condition: Your page doesn't hide any content but you want to improve the speed at which different parts of the page become interactive after server rendering.
evidence: And even if your page doesn't ever hide part of its content, you can still add always-visible Activity boundaries to improve hydration performance:
_original_recipe: Add always-visible Activity boundaries around components even when you never hide them, to improve hydration performance by letting React hydrate them as independent units.

recipe: (React 19.2+) For cleanup tied to an Activity visually hiding its content (e.g. pausing video), use useLayoutEffect instead of useEffect so the cleanup is not delayed by Suspense or a View Transition.
trigger_condition: When an Activity boundary hides a component that manages a video, audio, or iframe element and you need the cleanup to run synchronously with the visual change.
evidence: We call `useLayoutEffect` instead of `useEffect` because conceptually the clean-up code is tied to the component's UI being visually hidden.
_original_recipe: Use useLayoutEffect instead of useEffect when the cleanup is tied to a component being visually hidden by an Activity boundary, so the cleanup isn't delayed by Suspense or View Transitions.

recipe: (React 19.2+) A hidden Activity cleans up its children's Effects but keeps their DOM. For DOM with side effects (video, audio, iframe), add an Effect whose cleanup stops it, e.g. pauses the video.
trigger_condition: When a component inside an Activity boundary renders a video, audio, or iframe element and you want to prevent its side effect when the Activity is hidden.
evidence: If a component renders DOM that has a side effect, and you want to prevent that side effect when an Activity boundary hides it, add an Effect with a return function to clean it up.
_original_recipe: When using Activity in hidden mode, add an Effect with a cleanup function (return function) to any component that renders DOM with side effects like video, audio, or iframe, so the side effect stops when the component is hidden.

recipe: Refactor an Effect to perform its work in the returned cleanup function instead of relying on the effect mounting, because when an Activity is hidden all children's Effects are cleaned up.
trigger_condition: When an Activity is hidden and you are relying on an Effect mounting to clean up a component's side effects.
evidence: If you're relying on an Effect mounting to clean up a component's side effects, refactor the Effect to do the work in the returned cleanup function instead.
